recorded_candidate_concept.definition: The displayed or inferred title, heading, or caption that identifies the snapshot.
recorded_candidate_concept.rationale: Titles are usually the strongest single searchable description of a snapshot’s content and should be normalized across figures, tables, maps, and charts.
recorded_candidate_concept.sample_fields: table_title, figure_title, snapshot_title, chart_title, map_title, table_caption

limitations: The candidate concept examples do not enumerate all contributing profiles.
The assignments are later coverage-assessment evidence, not a hidden output of concept synthesis.
Terminological consolidation still requires review of differences between captions, internal headings, and panel titles.

outputs.recorded_v1_1_1_time_period_definition:
The period or date range represented by the data.

This field describes **when the represented data apply**. It does not describe when the snapshot artifact or parent document was created, prepared, issued, published, revised, or retrieved. When an explicit artifact date appears only as part of a footer or provenance statement, preserve the complete statement in `interpretive_note` rather than treating the date as `time_period`.

examples.title: Panel associations and table-header hierarchy
examples.teaching_objective: Recognize relationships that another flat field cannot preserve faithfully.

inputs.frozen_schema: v1.1.1, using a history-neutral model-facing presentation

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Panel-specific binding between each component of a composite snapshot and its applicable measured concept, time period, and visualization type.
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The snapshot is a composite figure with distinct panels: a map titled “Known Hazardous Areas and Number of Known Hazards as of 31 March 2016,” a donut chart titled “Types of Hazards - as of 31 March 2016,” a donut chart titled “MRE* Audiences: January - March 2016,” and a bar/line chart titled “Hazardous Areas Dec2013 - Mar2016.”
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The information describes how this snapshot’s own component panels relate to the variables, time periods, and visual encodings shown within the extracted figure, not administrative metadata about the parent document.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: The existing fields can record panel titles, an overall composite visualization type, multiple variable names, and multiple time periods, but they do not preserve which variable and time period belong to which panel. A flat representation could list “known hazards,” “types of hazards,” “MRE audiences,” “Dec2013 - Mar2016,” and “as of 31 March 2016” without retaining the panel-level associations.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: For a composite snapshot with multiple panels covering different measures and temporal scopes, users of the metadata record could misinterpret which date range or measured concept applies to which component if the panel relationships are not represented.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: Materiality is possible rather than certain because the snapshot image itself contains the panel labels, and v1.1.1 intentionally provides only coarse composite support through panel_title and visualization_type.

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Hierarchical grouping of table columns linking specific incident typologies to broader violation categories.
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The table title states it shows the distribution of incidents by typology and commune. The header is multi-level: commune rows are crossed with incident subtype columns, while spanning headers group those subtypes under broader categories such as “Violation du droit à la liberté,” “Violation du droit à biens,” “Violation du droit à la vie et à l’intégrité,” and “Violences sexuelles.”
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The grouped headers are part of the snapshot’s own table structure and define how the represented incident counts are classified; they are not administrative metadata about the parent document.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: The existing fields can record that columns represent incident typologies and can list both broad category labels and subtype labels, but they do not encode the parent-child or spanning-header relationship between a broad violation category and the specific incident types beneath it. Flattening all labels may make broad categories and subtypes appear as peer categories and lose the classification structure needed to interpret grouped columns.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: Without the grouping relationship, metadata-only interpretation or indexing could misrepresent which incident subtypes belong to each broader protection-violation class, impairing understanding of the table’s classification scheme and limiting discovery of snapshots organized around those broader incident categories.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: Possible rather than critical because v1.1.1 partially covers the information through category and dimension fields, and detailed header hierarchy may be considered closer to table-structure extraction than core snapshot metadata.

recorded_validation1_observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields identify the parent document title or underlying data source but do not represent a retrievable locator for the parent document.

recorded_validation1_candidates.definition: A URL, persistent link, or other retrievable locator for the parent source document or document landing page from which the snapshot was extracted.
recorded_validation1_candidates.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but cannot be used to retrieve or verify it, while data_source refers to the origin of the represented data rather than the parent document location.
recorded_validation1_candidates.operational_value: Supports retrieval, provenance verification, deduplication, and traceability from a snapshot record back to its source document.

outputs.human_adjudication_paraphrase: Parent-document retrieval metadata remains on the linked document record; no new snapshot field was accepted.

examples.title: Standards-informed derivation and attribution
examples.teaching_objective: Separate the origin of represented data from credit for producing the artifact.

recorded_observations.description: The named dataset, survey, or source data used to produce the table.
recorded_observations.reasoning: Data source names support provenance tracking and dataset-based discovery.

recorded_observations.description: The citation or provenance statement shown for the table.
recorded_observations.reasoning: Source citation documents provenance and helps assess reliability.

recorded_standards_decision.Candidate refinement: Split into flat `data_sources` and `attributions`; later introduce role-bearing objects
recorded_standards_decision.Rationale and v1.1.2 outcome: The distinction is semantically useful without requiring nesting. Preserve explicit attribution roles as flat source-grounded text.

recorded_final_field_specifications.Definition: The named datasets, surveys, publications, or other entities from which the represented data originate.
recorded_final_field_specifications.Standards alignment and usage guidance: Reflects the derivation distinction expressed by PROV-O `wasDerivedFrom` and DCMI `source`. Do not copy parent-document authors or publishers solely because they are associated with the document.

recorded_final_field_specifications.Definition: The agents explicitly credited with producing or contributing to the snapshot artifact.
recorded_final_field_specifications.Standards alignment and usage guidance: Reflects PROV-O `wasAttributedTo` and related Schema.org attribution properties. Preserve an explicit role together with the credited agent as a complete source-grounded expression.

limitations: The sample record is a two-field transcription from the paper, not a newly generated or independently evaluated extraction.
The 36-to-37 change clarifies an overloaded provenance field; it was not a new requirement accepted in held-out validation.
The standards review was interactive and human-adjudicated. No fixed historical prompt or automated pipeline is supplied.
